newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks rally at close, pierce 700.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks rally at close, pierce 700.

text.p: Argentine stocks charged higher Monday and pierced the 700 mark on the leading index for the first time in three years.
Dealers said the market was ruling out a U.S. interest rate hike this week and betting on strong January tax revenue.
"Players have latched onto local factors such as strong forecasts for tax revenue and company profits," said Emilio Alessandro of brokers Alessandro. "The mood is bullish."
The blue-chip MerVal .MERV index jumped 2.0 percent to 706.19, boosting a five-day rally to 7.6 percent.
It last closed above 700 on February 4, 1994.
"The market is drawing strength from the heavyweight telephone sector and liquidity is good," said another trader.

Telefonica and Telecom, which received a host of foreign buy recommendations after a telephone tariff change late Thursday, stretched Friday's surge with new gains of 2.3 percent and 1.3 percent, respectively.

January tax revenue came in after the market close at $4.36 billion against a consensus forecast of $4.01 billion and collection of $3.87 billion in January 1996. "From now on weekly data will be closely scrutinized to see if there is a growth trend," the trader said.
Floor volume eased to 27.6 million pesos Monday compared to 28.2 million Friday, while over-the-counter deals slowed to 124.1 million pesos from 151.9 million Friday.
The broad market index advanced 1.3 percent, with winners smashing losers 57 to seven and 14 issues closing flat.

Top main-tier performers were oil firm Astra, carmaker Ciadea and power utility Central Costanera, which shot up 5.3 percent, 4.9 percent and 3.8 percent, respectively. The only MerVal losers were pulp maker Celulosa, down 1.2 percent, and gas company Transportadora de Gas del Sur, off 0.4 percent.
